newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's parliament adopts new telecom law.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's parliament adopts new telecom law.

text.p: Serbia's parliament adopted on Wednesday a law separating posts from telecommunications in its monopoly PTT Srbije, clearing a path to privatisation of Serbian telecommunications to foreigners.

The division of those activities will create conditions for a faster development of both sectors and create environment for more inflow of foreign capital, Serbian Transportation Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic told parliament.
By law, PTT Srbije can be established as a holding company, but the law does not oblige it to do so, Kostadinovic added.
"The law creates legal possibilities for restructuring and ownership transformation of the PTT Srbije," the minister said.
"The government wants to urgently create a legal environment for an inflow of foreign capital," the minister said addressing the parliament.
The law also envisages a possibility to sell the new company's capital in the form of shares to foreign investors.
The government however fell short of specifying in the document that any sale of shares to foreigners will be conducted via public tenders.
Commentators said this was because the government has already identified a preferred candidate -- the Italian state telecommunications monopoly Stet.
But the minister insisted all bidders will be treated equally.
"The bidder who offers the best conditions will be chosen as a partner. The government will make the final decision on the most successful bidder," the minister told Reuters.
Kostadinovic said foreign companies were growing impatient over lack of law regulating investment and privatisation in the telecommunications sector.
"Foreign negotiators become nervous because they are ready to invest but we have insufficiently precise legal procedure," Kostadinovic added.
The minister also said the government will retain a majority stake not only in PTT Srbije but in any other big state monopoly.
The law separating posts from telecommunications will not immediately bring more competition in a lucrative mobile telephony sector.

"The law creates a possibility for PTT Srbije to become a holding of two companies and a possibility to develop telephony and telecommunications in line with ongoing world developments. We have yet to see whether there will be a possibility to create other companies," Kostadinovic said.
Serbian privatisation minister Milan Beko said the postal part of the new holding company will not immediately be possible to privatise.
"Posts are highly subsidised activities around the world, they first need to be restructured in order to become more efficient and then embark on privatisation," Beko said.
According to previous government announcements, posts were supposed to remain state-controlled while telecommunications would be offered to investors.
Kostadinovic said the new law was a part of a wider Serbian government's 1997 economic policy, which had anticipated the bill by September.
"We have adopted the law in time and now it's up to PTT Srbije to make it operational," the minister said. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
